Notes: OOP_Using_Java- Introduction to Java

Introduction to Java
  • Java is a high level, object oriented prorgramming languages widely used for developing various types of applications like Web applications, Web services, Mobile apps, Games etc.
  • It was originally devloped by Sun Microsystem in year 1995. Presently it is owned by Oracle.
  • Its main feature that makes it so popular is that it can run on various platforms like Windows, Unix, various versions of Linux as well as Mac operating system. 
Features of Java
Following are the main features of Java.
NoFeatureDetails
1Object orientedJava is pure object oriented programming language. It supports all features of Object oriented programming. Everything in Java is an object. In fact, it is more object oriented than C++ because Java doesn't support many non-object oriented features like friend functions, global data and global functions which are present in C++. These features, in fact violate the some basic principles of object oriented programming and can create major security issues hence they are not supported by Java.
2Platform independent
Portable
Architecture neutral 		Java code is not compiled to any specific operating system. Hence it can be compiled once and run on various operating systems. This makes Java platform independent.
3Simple (Easy to learn)Java doesn't support many features which were present in previous languages, that were not really needed widely and make programming more complicated and error prone. These features are friend functions, operator overloading, multiple inheritance, global data and functions etc. Hence it is very easy to learn Java and makes programming simple, without losing major programming capabilities.
4SecureJava doesn't work directly with the operating system. It is not directly responsible for allocation and de-allocation of memory. This completely avoids situations where the program terminates abruptly due to errors related to memory access. Hence it is more secure and safe.
5RobustJava is a type safe language. It has strong compile time error checking. It also supports exception handling which is a strong mechanism for run time error checking. These features make it more robust during execution. 
6Multi-threadedJava supports multi-threading which allows the program to run simultaneously on more than one fronts. It can also handle synchronization, inter-thread communication and deadlocks. When used properly, this feature can increase the throughput of your program.
7High performanceThe second stage compilation of Java code optimizes it highly to the native code. Hence it runs faster than other interpreted languages. However, it is definitely slower in execution than other languages like C, C++ which are directly compiled to native code in single step itself.
8DistributedJava support communication between two machines that are connected either by intranet or by internet. Hence, it can be used for developing software system whose parts are distributed over a network or even internet. 
9DynamicClasses in Java can be loaded on demand while the program is running. This makes it a dynamic language.
Two stage compilation
Programs written in any language must be converted to machine language. This task is done by the compiler of that language and the process is called as compilation of program. The compiler first checks if the program is written as per the rules of that language (called as syntax). If there are errors, it lists all the errors along with meaningful error messages. Such errors are called as compile-time errors. Only when the program is syntactically correct, it gets converted to machine language. So the compiler has two tasks to do:
  1. Check if the program is syntactically correct. If not, it lists all compile-time errors. 
  2. If yes, it converts the code to native language.

If both these tasks are done entirely by the compiler during compilation, it is called as single-stage compilation. This is done in languages like C, C++ etc. 
However, such model of compilation has a major limitation. The compiled code is specific to the operating system and underlying machine architecture, which together are called as Platform. Hence, it won't work directly on other platforms. We need to re-compile the code to generate platform specific native code and then run on that platform. This is shown in diagram below: 
Single stage compilation model of languages like C and C++

​

​

Compilation for languages like C and C++ is specific to the platform on which the compilation is done. Hence the compiled code can’t be directly used on other platforms.

2 stage compilation model of Java

​​​​​​​​
Source code of java gets compiled by its compiler (javac) into platform independant bytecode. This bytecode then gets converted into platform specific machine code during the second stage compilation. Hence the bytecode of java is platform independant. However, note that the JVM itself must be platform dependant as it have to generate platform dependant machine code.

Installing JDK
JDK stands for Java development kit. It contains the java compiler, java virtual machine, Java run-time enviroment as well as many other libraries and utilities. This is the basic software needs on developers machine for developing any java software. 
JDK can be installed by following the steps given below:
1Go to https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/

​
  • Here note that there are various version of JDK available for download. It is recommended to download the latest stable version from this list.
  • Also notice that different JDK is available for different operating systems and platforms. We should download that JDK which suits your operating system and platform.
  • Select the JDK that suits your operating system and start the download
2For winodws platform, the JDK is available for installation in two options.
  • executable setup file: jdk-22_windows-x64_bin.exe (sha256):
    This is a setup program that will copy the jdk folder in windows system directory.
  • Zip file: jdk-22_windows-x64_bin.zip (sha256)
    This is simple a zip that we can un-zip to any folder of our choice.
The first option is specific to windows operating system. Hence, we will prefer the second option of zip file as it is common for other operating systems also.

First Java program
This is a simple Hello World program in java. Follow the steps given below.
1Create a directory for storing java source. For Example: C:\Object\courses\java\Code\Demo
We will call this as our source directory.
2Create a new text file using any text editor and write the code given below. Save this file in the source directory with the name First.java

public class First 
{
    // This is single line comment
    /*
        This is multi-line comment
    */
   public static void main(String []args) 
   {
      System.out.println("Hello World"); 
   }
}		Note:
  1. main is entry point function
  2. It is declared as public and static
  3. Its return type of void
  4. Hello World is the string to be displayed on console. It is passed as parameter to the function println which is called on System.out which represents the primary console of the system.
3Open command prompt > Change dir to the source directory and run the follwing command to compile the java program:
> javac First.java
This will generate a file First.class in the source directory, as follows:

​
This is the first step compilation which converts the source code in First.java file to bytecode and saves in First.class file.
4Now run the First.class file using following command to see the output of the program.

​
Note that while running a class file, we DON'T include the extension .class in the command.

Path and Classpath
PATH:
Note that when we ask windows operating system to run a program in windows, it searches for the executable file in a predefined list of directories. This list of directories in set as PATH variable in windows operating system.
We can set the path in two ways:
1Setting path locally only for current command prompt

> set path=%path%;C:\Object\software\java\jdk-22\bin
​
Here %path% is the current value of path. We add one more directory (C:\Object\software\java\jdk-22\bin) to the path using this command

You can check the updated value of PATH using following commnd:
> echo %path%
​
See the new path getting appended at the end.
Note that this setting is applicable ONLY for the current instance of command prompt. It is not applicable to other applications, other command prompts opened elsewhere as well as new command prompts created later.
2Setting PATH at system level

This is done as per the steps mentioned in the topic "Installing JDK". 
Note that this setting is permanent and applicable at system level. Only those applications which are already running at the time of this setting, need to restart to get these changes.

CLASSPATH:
This is the list of directories in which JVM searches .class files. When we run a command (say >java xyz), 
java searches for xyz.class file in the directories which are listed in the classpath variable one by one till it is found. This value can also be set in two ways:
 
1Setting classpath locally only for current command prompt

> set classpath=%classpath%;C:\Object\courses\java\Code\Demo

We can even check the classpath value by
> echo %classpath%


Here %classpath% is the current value of classpath. We add one more directory (C:\Object\courses\java\Code\Demo) to the classpath using this command

​
2Setting CLASSPATH at system level

This is done as per the steps mentioned in the topic "Installing JDK". Just note that we have to create a new variable with name classpath and then assign the value. 
Note that this setting is permanent and applicable at system level. Only those applications which are already running at the time of this setting, need to restart to get these changes.


JDK, JVM and JRE
JVM stands for Java Virtual Machine. It is the run-time environment in which the class files execute. 
​​​​​​​
Major responsibilities of JVM are:
  1. Request the classloader of JRE to load the .class file when the class is used for the first time.
  2. Interpret the bytecode and execute it.
  3. Initialize the static variables of that class by executing the code and all static blocks from top to bottom in that class.
  4. Create the object of class Class. This object can be used to get all information related to the class through reflection. Reference of this class object can be obtained by class className.getClass() 
  5. Perform garbage collection operation for un-referenced objects.

What is JVM, JRE and JDK
  • JVM is Java virtual machine in which java programs get executed. It converts byte code to native code and hence it is platform dependant.
  • JRE is Java Runtime Environment which consists of JVM + core classes and supporting files
  • JDK is Java Development Kit which consists of JRE+ all development tools needed by programmers
​
Note that JVM alone can't be installed. Hence we have to install JRE on client side to run the java software. We need various developemt tools like compiler, debugger and Java docs etc in addition to JRE for development of software. Hence we install JDK on developer's side.

​​​​​​​Classloader:
Java classloader is part of the JRE which load classes into JVM whenever needed at runtime. If the required class is not found, it throws ClassNotFoundException.
